A short talk about what a statistical programmer does in a methods group, using my work on the [MAMS](../../software.qmd#mams) package as the example. It covers:

- what goes into a [pkgdown](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/) site and how one is built from a package's help files and vignettes;
- the [MAMS documentation site](https://tjaki.github.io/MAMS/) we built this way;
- interactive output in slides, shown with a Plotly animation of the central limit theorem;
- [webR](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/latest/), which runs R inside the browser, so readers can edit and run MAMS examples without installing anything.

On webR, the gains are near-native speed in the browser and nothing to install, neither R on the reader's computer nor a server. The limits at the time were that not every CRAN package was available, code runs on a single core, and access to local files is restricted.

The slides are a Quarto revealjs presentation styled after the BSU template, with a live webR console. They are embedded below; press `F` for full screen, or [open them in a new tab](https://nikotinz.github.io/BSU_Together_Talk/). R takes a few seconds to load before the code cells run.
